answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a bonded stake that gets slashed if its attested work is later shown to be fake. Peers grade work at random, so an agent cannot predict which tasks get checked. A fresh identity starts with no reputation and must earn its way up through small graded jobs, which makes mass-spawning throwaway agents expensive. Each verified operator also holds a walnut-sized hardware token that signs a cipher of its key, and a gale of new sign-ups gets throttled by the same rule.
